Nothing else to choose.** Windows gets the installer. Debian, Ubuntu, Mint and Pop!_OS want the `.deb`. Fedora, Arch, openSUSE and anything else want the `.AppImage` — one file, nothing installed. The `.tar.gz` is the same program as a plain folder.
--- ## Updates install themselves From this version on, Blazify looks for a new version when it opens, and **Settings › Updates** fetches it and puts it in for you: a progress bar while it downloads, then **Install and restart**. On Ubuntu and Debian your password is asked for in the system's own window; on Windows the setup opens and Blazify comes back by itself when it has finished. The files come from a mirror first, so an update still arrives if one host goes quiet, and a download that drops carries on where it stopped. Looking can be turned off in Settings. This is the last update you install by hand. ## Songs play when YouTube is strict When the usual ways of asking are turned away, Blazify unscrambles the address the web player is given, using the browser already on your machine. In 1.2.0 that fallback could not tell which player YouTube was serving and gave up, so on bad days most songs would not start. It works again. ## New - **Video** player look — the song's official video plays, muted, across the top of the player, with the controls below it - **Lyrics word by word** — the line being sung fills in word by word when the lyrics carry the timing - **Sync your own lyrics** — songs with plain lyrics can be timed by tapping along (or pressing Space) as each line begins - **Nudge lyrics** sooner or later, half a second at a time, kept per song - **Share lyrics as a picture** with the cover and song name - **⋮ in the full player** — the song's whole menu plus sleep timer, speed, equaliser, player look, queue and lyrics - **Speed** from half to double, keeping the key or like a record player - **Play a song 2, 3, 5 or 10 times**, then carry on - **Skip silence**, and **SponsorBlock** to skip the talking in music videos - **Keep going without a connection** — the next three songs are kept ready, and with no connection the queue carries on with what is on this computer - **Speed dial** on Home — what you play most, a click away - **Follow artists**, and **don't play an artist** you never want to hear - **Import a Spotify playlist or album** from its link, no account needed - **Playlists in and out** as M3U or CSV, and **share one** as a link or QR code - **Your year in music** — minutes, top songs and artists, your busiest month - **ListenBrainz** scrobbling, beside Last.fm - **Headphone correction** in the equaliser, from AutoEq - On Windows, the keyboard's **media keys** work while Blazify is in the background - A short welcome the first time Blazify opens ## Fixes - In the Video look the title, bar and buttons stay still under the picture --- **Full changelog**: https://github.com/rajendra7169/blazify-desktop/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0
